task_description: The team must determine how many edits were made to the English Wikipedia page 'Antidisestablishmentarianism' from the page's creation until the end of June 2023. The gold answer, 2732, is the cumulative count of all revisions to that article through 2023-06-30 inclusive.
final_vs_expected: produced None (run hit the 30-message cap with no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 2732 — the team converged internally on 2,735 (off by 3) but never routed to Finalizer to emit it.
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: after the Critic asked for evidence, the selector LLM looped on WebResearcher for ~25 straight turns and never picked the Finalizer, so the run timed out with no FINAL ANSWER despite a near-correct internal consensus.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): the run had a near-final number (2,735) by Turn 2 and a Critic sign-off on the arithmetic by Turn 3, yet the selector never routed to Finalizer; turns 5-29 produce no progress and no FINAL ANSWER, ending only at the message cap. 1.3 (Step repetition): WebResearcher republishes '2,735' verbatim across ~20 turns (5,8,10,11,14,15,16,17,18-29) without new work. 3.2 (No/incomplete verification): the Critic at Turn 3 explicitly demands the underlying page-info and full paginated API count be shown ('the 84 figure is solid'), but no agent ever re-fetches or re-counts — the verification request is satisfied only in form (restated numbers) not substance. 2.5 (Ignored other agent's input): the Critic's concrete request — 'confirm the exact count of revisions strictly after 2023-06-30 and show that the API result was fully paginated' — is never acted on; WebResearcher's reasoning at Turn 4 even concedes 'the evidence provided only supports arithmetic calculations' but then just agrees rather than fetching, and selector reasoning repeatedly says it needs 'actual outputs' yet keeps re-picking the same agent that won't produce them.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector picks WebResearcher, which runs a 9-round private loop. It searches, hits XTools (blocked by an anti-bot 'Anubis' wall), then succeeds via the MediaWiki API. It reads page-info 'Total number of edits: 2,819' (as of 2026-06-02) and queries revisions after 2023-07-01 (rvdir=newer). Its round-9 reasoning notes a 'newer query returned a value of 65' but it 'want[s] to count the list length manually'; it then publishes that there are '84 edits after June 2023' and computes 2,819 − 84 = 2,735. Turn 2: Selector picks Analyst, which does no independent computation — it restates the WebResearcher's numbers and republishes 2,735. Turn 3: Selector picks Critic, which correctly flags that the raw page-info/API outputs were never shown, that the '84' was not demonstrated to be a full paginated count, and that the 'inception until June 2023' = through 2023-06-30 inclusive boundary needs care. It asks the Analyst/WebResearcher to re-derive and show the count. Turns 4-29: Selector re-picks WebResearcher almost every turn. WebResearcher never re-fetches or re-counts; it emits empties (turns 5, 9) and bare or hedged restatements of '2,735' (turns 8, 10, 11, 14-29). The selector's reasoning each turn says it needs 'actual outputs'/'evidence' but keeps routing back to the same agent and never selects the Finalizer. The run hits the 30-message cap at Turn 29 with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is overwhelmingly a structural/harness non-convergence failure, not genuine inter-agent misalignment. The team actually reached a coherent, near-correct internal consensus (2,735 vs gold 2,732) by Turn 2, and the Critic raised a legitimate, well-targeted verification demand at Turn 3. The fatal breakdown is in the selector control loop: from Turn 4 onward the selector routes to WebResearcher ~25 consecutive times, its private reasoning each turn correctly diagnosing that it needs 'actual outputs / evidence' to satisfy the Critic — yet it never (a) selects the Finalizer to lock in the answer, nor (b) chooses a strategy that would actually produce the missing evidence (e.g., Analyst with run_python to paginate/count). WebResearcher, meanwhile, has fully exited its tool-using mode: after Turn 4 it runs only 1 trivial model round per turn and just republishes the number, so the loop can never break. The substantive answer error (2,735 vs 2,732, off by 3) is a separate single-agent capability issue: WebResearcher's '84 edits after June 2023' count was eyeballed from a truncated API dump (its own reasoning admits the newer query 'returned a value of 65' and it wanted to 'count the list length manually'), and the total '2,819' was taken from live page-info dated 2026 with no proof of pagination. But that 3-edit error is moot because the run never emits any answer. Misalignment signal is weak: the Critic's input IS ignored (2.5), but this is driven by selector mis-routing and WebResearcher's degenerate behavior rather than an agent distorting or withholding information it privately knew.
reasoning_vs_published: Private-vs-published gaps are minor here. (a) Mild distortion at Turn 1: WebResearcher's round-9 reasoning says 'The newer query returned a value of 65' yet it publishes '84 edits after June 2023' — the published number diverges from a figure its own reasoning surfaced, with no shown reconciliation (a lossy/uncertain count presented as firm, contributing to the off-by-3 error). It also privately flags it should 'count the list length manually to verify' but publishes the unverified count anyway. (b) Turn 4 WebResearcher reasoning concedes 'the evidence provided only supports arithmetic calculations, rather than underlying counts' and that it 'should confirm that they are correct and that further verification is necessary' — its published message duly agrees that counts are 'not fully verified,' but it never does the verification its own reasoning identifies as needed (reasoning-acknowledged gap, no action). (c) The Critic's published demand is precise and correct ('confirm the exact count of revisions strictly after 2023-06-30 and show that the API result was fully paginated... so the 84 figure is solid'), and downstream agents simply never act on it. (d) The selector's reasoning is the clearest signal: it repeatedly states the right diagnosis — e.g. Turn 8 'they didn't actually gather any new information—just restated what was already known... we really need the web researcher to provide actual outputs this time' — yet keeps selecting the same non-productive agent and never the Finalizer, so its reasoning and its routing action are themselves mismatched.
